label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=8)
explanation: Fires essentially only at the delimiter step (99.9% of activations, ~100% of mass), i.e. the step that outputs the first original token. It never fires during the original phase, and almost never in the copy phase (7 dev activations). Within delimiter steps the firing rate and magnitude rise steeply with sequence length: rate ~0 for L<=5, 3% at L=6, 8% at L=7, 26% at L=8, 42% at L=9; L>=8 carries ~90% of mass. Which long sequences fire depends on content in a graded, distributed way. It is boosted when the first token (the one being output) is n, f, h, 0, i, u or x, and when the prefix contains many of k, p, t, r, a, o; sequences heavy in z, e, m, c tend not to fire. No single token rule captures this. Adding first-token or token-count conditions only raised dev F1 from 0.49 to about 0.52, so the simple length-gated delimiter predicate is the one recorded. Precision is low (about a third of L>=8 delimiter steps fire).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: n, h, f, 0, i, u; least: y, -, k, t) and the third original token (most: p, k, r, a, o, t; least: i, u, v, h); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=9, phase=1, recall_idx=0.
